builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: TextSeal2: Distortion-Free LLM Watermarking with Copula Mixing and Memoryless Races
summary: Replaces TextSeal's coin-flip key routing (and textGrain's post-logits optimization) with a single virtual key merged via Gaussian copula, plus a memoryless exponential race that keeps the signal intact under speculative decoding. Costs are reported as negligible: no measurable inference latency, no loss of output diversity, and no change in speculative acceptance rate, though it adds key-management and detector-side complexity. It can fail if watermarking is not a production requirement, if adversaries paraphrase or edit the text enough to erase the signal, or if the detection gains do not transfer to the reader's model, decoding stack, or text lengths.
rationale: The method is inference-time and cheap enough for constrained infrastructure, but watermarking only matters if the reader must prove text provenance, so workload-specific validation of detection rates on their own model and speculative-decoding setup is required before adoption.

claims.statement: Replaces TextSeal's coin-flip key routing (and textGrain's post-logits optimization) with a single virtual key merged via Gaussian copula, plus a memoryless exponential race that keeps the signal intact under speculative decoding. Costs are reported as negligible: no measurable inference latency, no loss of output diversity, and no change in speculative acceptance rate, though it adds key-management and detector-side complexity. It can fail if watermarking is not a production requirement, if adversaries paraphrase or edit the text enough to erase the signal, or if the detection gains do not transfer to the reader's model, decoding stack, or text lengths.

At equal output diversity, detects 8–22 percentage points more 100-token answers than TextSeal at 10^-3 false-positive rate; under speculative decoding, detects 18 and 22 points more 200-token answers than TextSeal and textGrain at unchanged acceptance rate.
